mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate triggers a forward discounting effect, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) exceeding 2,000 in 3 months reduces consumer purchasing power, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in rising-benefits periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
